intro: Professionals and everyday users convert gallons (us) (gal (US)) to quarts (us) (qt) when working across us_customary and us_customary standards in culinary recipe scaling, beverage bottling, laboratory reagent preparation, and fluid tank capacity sizing. One gallon (us liquid) equals 4 quarts (us), while 1 quart (us liquid) equals 0.25 gallons (us). Whether you are verifying volume & liquid specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many quarts (us) (qt) are in 1 gallon (us liquid) (gal (US))?
faqs.answer: There are 4 quarts (us) (qt) in 1 gallon (us liquid) (gal (US)), which rounds to 4 qt for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 quart (us liquid) equals 0.25 gallons (us).

faqs.question: How do I convert gallons (us) to quarts (us) (gal (US) to qt)?
faqs.answer: To convert gallons (us) to quarts (us), use the formula: qt = gal (US) × 4. For example, converting 5 gal (US) gives 20 qt.

faqs.question: What is 5 gallons (us) in quarts (us)?
faqs.answer: 5 gallons (us) (gal (US)) equals exactly 20 quarts (us) (qt) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
